The Python logo (public/vendor/python-logo-notext.svg)
======================================================

The Python logo is a TRADEMARK of the Python Software Foundation. It is not
covered by an open-source licence the way the pandas logo in the sister
data-science repo is — that one is BSD-3-Clause, a copyright licence. Copyright
and trademark are different questions, and this is the trademark one.

The PSF Trademark Usage Policy (https://www.python.org/psf/trademarks/) says, in
the parts that bear on a course thumbnail:

  * "Non-commercial uses to promote the Python programming language are
    allowed" for the unaltered logo.
  * Nominative use — "stating accurately that software is written in the Python
    programming language ... is always allowed".
  * "Any other commercial uses require prior written permission from PSF."
  * The logo "should be ... accompanied by a symbol for unregistered
    trademarks: '(TM)' or a small TM".

How it is used here
-------------------
* The logo is UNALTERED. It is not recoloured, cropped, restyled or combined
  with other marks.
* It is accompanied by a TM, as the policy asks.
* It is used nominatively, to name the language the course teaches. The
  course's own identity is the GraphL wordmark and the FULL COURSE badge; the
  cover does not suggest the PSF produced, endorsed or sponsored it.

What still needs a decision
---------------------------
If the video is MONETISED, that is a commercial use, and the policy asks for
prior written permission from the PSF. Using the logo on a monetised channel
without that permission is outside what the policy grants.

Requests go to the PSF Trademarks Committee. If permission is not sought or not
granted, rebuild the cover with the repo's own glyph instead:

    npm run thumb:film -- --mark glyph

which draws the `>>>` REPL prompt — Python's most recognisable screen element,
owned by nobody.
